summary: special_coul is applied by scaling the whole damped-shifted-force Coulomb term by factor_coul instead of subtracting (1-factor_coul)*prefactor as the CPU style does, so forces and Coulomb energies on special-bonded pairs are wrong.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:223-229 compute_fcoul: 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = factor_coul * qqrd2e * qtmp * q(j);' ... 'return prefactor * (erfcc/r + 2.0*alpha_kk/MY_PIS * erfcd + r*f_shift_kk) * r2inv;' and :248-253 compute_ecoul: 'const KK_FLOAT prefactor = factor_coul * qqrd2e * qtmp * q(j);' ... 'return prefactor * (erfcc - r*e_shift_kk - rsq*f_shift_kk) / r;'. CPU base src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf.cpp:137-143 'prefactor = qqrd2e*qtmp*q[j]/r; forcecoul = prefactor * (erfcc/r + 2.0*alpha/MY_PIS * erfcd + r*f_shift) * r; if (factor_coul < 1.0) forcecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;' and :164-165 'ecoul = prefactor * (erfcc - r*e_shift - rsq*f_shift); if (factor_coul < 1.0) ecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;'. Algebraically CPU gives A*S - (1-fc)*A/r while the kokkos style gives fc*A*S (A = qqrd2e*qi*qj, S = erfcc/r + 2a/sqrt(pi)*erfcd + r*f_shift); they agree only when factor_coul == 1. The correctly ported sibling src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:205-215 and :258-262 uses the CPU form.
failure_scenario: Any molecular system with special_bonds coul != 1.0 (the LAMMPS default 0.0 0.0 0.0) run with 'pair_style lj/cut/coul/dsf/kk': every 1-2/1-3/1-4 pair inside cut_coul gets a Coulomb force and energy different from pair_style lj/cut/coul/dsf, e.g. with factor_coul = 0 the kk style returns exactly 0 while the CPU style returns -A*(S-1/r).
suggested_fix: Set prefactor = qqrd2e*qtmp*q(j)/r (no factor_coul), form forcecoul/ecoul as in the CPU style and then apply 'if (factor_coul < 1.0) forcecoul -= (1.0-factor_coul)*prefactor;' (same for ecoul), mirroring pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp. The same defect is in src/KOKKOS/pair_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:260-266 and should be fixed together.

summary: The DSF self-energy is added only to the global eng_coul and never to the per-atom energy array, so eatom/compute pe/atom is missing the self term that the CPU style tallies.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:129-133 'for (int ii = 0; ii < inum; ii ++) { double qtmp = atom->q[ii]; eng_coul += -(e_shift/2.0 + alpha/MY_PIS) * qtmp*qtmp*static_cast<double>(qqrd2e); }' -- there is no corresponding d_eatom/eatom update anywhere in the file (the only eatom handling is the sync at :151-154). CPU base src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf.cpp:110-112 'if (eflag) { double e_self = -(e_shift/2.0 + alpha/MY_PIS) * qtmp*qtmp*qqrd2e; ev_tally(i,i,nlocal,0,0.0,e_self,0.0,0.0,0.0,0.0); }', and Pair::ev_tally with i==j and newton_pair==0 adds 0.5*e_self twice, i.e. the full e_self, to eatom[i]. The correctly ported sibling src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:145-153 does 'if (eflag_atom) { ... for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++) eatom[i] += -(e_shift/2.0 + alpha/MY_PIS) * qisq * force->qqrd2e; }'.
failure_scenario: 'pair_style lj/cut/coul/dsf/kk' + 'compute pe/atom' (or a dump with c_pe): the sum over per-atom energies does not equal the reported global potential energy and differs from the CPU style by -(e_shift/2 + alpha/sqrt(pi))*qqrd2e*sum(q_i^2), which for a charged system is a large fraction of the Coulomb energy.
suggested_fix: After 'k_eatom.sync_host()' add a loop that adds the per-atom self-energy to eatom[i] for i < nlocal, guarded by eflag_atom, exactly as pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp does.

summary: The host-side self-energy loop reads the host charge array atom->q without ever calling atomKK->sync(Host,Q_MASK), so on a GPU build it reads charges that are stale after the device-side atom exchange/sort.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:96 only does 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read)' (execution_space is Device for the /kk and /kk/device variants), and then :131 reads the host raw pointer 'double qtmp = atom->q[ii];'. atom->q is the host mirror of atomKK->k_q (src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_charge_kokkos.cpp:73 'memoryKK->grow_kokkos(atomKK->k_q,atomKK->q,nmax,"atom:q")'). Both AtomVecKokkos::unpack_exchange_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_kokkos.cpp:2852 'atomKK->modified(space,datamask_exchange);') and AtomVecChargeKokkos::sort_kokkos (src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_charge_kokkos.cpp:122-134, Sorter.sort(...,d_q) then 'atomKK->modified(Device, ALL_MASK & ~F_MASK)') mark q modified on the device, and nothing in the /kk force path syncs it back to the host.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank GPU run where atoms migrate: after comm->exchange() the host q array still holds the previous step's atom set and count, so the self-energy sum uses wrong charges (and reads past the previously valid nlocal entries), corrupting the reported Coulomb energy.
suggested_fix: Either call atomKK->sync(Host,Q_MASK) before the loop, or (better) compute the self-energy in a Kokkos parallel_reduce over the device view q, adding to ev.ecoul / d_eatom.

summary: The self-energy loop is not guarded by eflag and indexes the charge array with the neighbor-list slot ii instead of list->ilist[ii], and it uses list->inum instead of nlocal.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:127-133 'int inum = list->inum; for (int ii = 0; ii < inum; ii ++) { //int i = list->ilist[ii];\n  double qtmp = atom->q[ii]; eng_coul += ...; }' -- the correct index line is commented out. CPU base src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf.cpp:110 wraps the self term in 'if (eflag)' and uses qtmp = q[i] with i = ilist[ii]. The sibling src/KOKKOS/pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:119-123 loops 'for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++)'.
failure_scenario: Currently benign because NPairKokkos sets d_ilist(i)=i and inum=nlocal (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:593,:356), and eng_coul is reset by ev_init on every eflag_global step; but the unconditional accumulation dirties eng_coul on non-energy steps and the ii indexing silently breaks if a future neighbor build ever produces a non-identity ilist.
suggested_fix: Guard the loop with 'if (eflag)' (splitting the eflag_global and eflag_atom contributions), and loop 'for (int i = 0; i < nlocal; i++)' as pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp does.

summary: The DSF self-energy is added to eng_coul only and never to the per-atom energy array, so per-atom energies are missing the self term the CPU style tallies through ev_tally(i,i,...). The same loop is also unguarded by eflag and indexes atom->q by the neighbour-list slot ii rather than ilist[ii].
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:127-133 vs src/EXTRA-PAIR/pair_lj_cut_coul_dsf.cpp:110-112; the correct sibling pair_born_coul_dsf_kokkos.cpp:145-153 adds the self term to eatom under eflag_atom).

summary: The block that undoes the 'pair/only' sort/atom-map overrides is guarded by 'if (lmp->pair_only_flag)' instead of 'if (!lmp->pair_only_flag)', so 'package kokkos pair/only on' never actually moves atom sorting and the atom map back to the host.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:776-785 sets 'if (lmp->pair_only_flag) { if (sort_legacy == 0) { sort_legacy = 1; sort_changed = 1; } if (atom_map_legacy == 0) { atom_map_legacy = 1; atom_map_changed = 1; } }'; then src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:824-833 immediately does 'if (lmp->pair_only_flag) { if (sort_changed) { sort_legacy = 0; sort_changed = 0; } if (atom_map_changed) { atom_map_legacy = 0; atom_map_changed = 0; } }'. The analogous 'change them back' block for the comm flags at line 789 is correctly guarded with 'if (gpu_aware_flag && !lmp->pair_only_flag)'. As written the second block is only reachable when pair_only_flag is true, i.e. exactly when the first block has just set the flags, so the two cancel and the settings never change; and when pair/only is later switched off the stale sort_changed/atom_map_changed flags can never be undone (they were already cleared).
failure_scenario: GPU build, 'package kokkos pair/only on': the intent is that with only pair styles accelerated the atom sort and atom map run on the host (sort_legacy = atom_map_legacy = 1). Instead both stay 0 and sorting/atom map keep running on the device while all non-pair styles are plain CPU styles, costing extra host/device transfers (and exercising the device sort/map path that pair/only is meant to avoid).
suggested_fix: Change the condition at line 824 to 'if (!lmp->pair_only_flag)' so the sort/atom-map overrides are undone only when pair/only is turned off again, matching the comm-flag block at line 789.

summary: The SLURM_LOCALID branch of the '-k on g N' parser is missing the 'if (ngpus > 0)' guard that all six other MPI-launcher branches have, so 'g 0' divides by zero.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:223-228: 'if ((str = getenv("SLURM_LOCALID"))) { int local_rank = std::stoi(str); device = local_rank % ngpus; if (device >= skip_gpu) device++; set_flag = 1; }' -- no ngpus check, while FLUX_TASK_LOCAL_ID (229), MPT_LRANK (237), MV2_COMM_WORLD_LOCAL_RANK (245), OMPI_COMM_WORLD_LOCAL_RANK (253), PMI_LOCAL_RANK (261) and PALS_LOCAL_RANKID (269) all wrap the identical body in 'if (ngpus > 0) { ... }'. ngpus comes straight from the user at line 208 and is only rejected later (line 316) for LMP_KOKKOS_GPU builds, and 'ngpus > 0' is not required at all for host-only builds (line 209-212 only errors for ngpus > 0).
failure_scenario: Run under SLURM (SLURM_LOCALID set) with 'lmp -k on g 0 ...' (e.g. a host-only Kokkos build where the user disables GPUs explicitly, or a typo): 'local_rank % 0' is integer division by zero -> SIGFPE/undefined behavior before any of the later argument validation runs.
suggested_fix: Wrap the SLURM_LOCALID body in 'if (ngpus > 0) { ... }' exactly like the other launcher branches, or validate ngpus >= 1 right after parsing it.

summary: The 't'/'threads' command-line option reads arg[iarg+1] without the 'if (iarg+2 > narg)' bounds check that the 'd'/'device' and 'g'/'gpus' options perform.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:282-289: '} else if (strcmp(arg[iarg],"t") == 0 || strcmp(arg[iarg],"threads") == 0) { nthreads = utils::inumeric(FLERR, arg[iarg+1], false, lmp);' -- compare src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:200-202 ('if (iarg+2 > narg) error->all(FLERR,"Invalid Kokkos command-line args");') and :207. narg here is kklast-kkfirst computed in src/lammps.cpp:302-304, so arg[iarg+1] can be one past the delimited range.
failure_scenario: 'lmp -k on t' as the final command-line arguments passes narg=1; arg[1] is read out of the delimited range (it is argv's terminating nullptr for a main()-provided argv, but an arbitrary pointer for a library caller of lammps_open() whose argv is not nullptr-terminated) -> out-of-bounds read instead of the intended 'Invalid Kokkos command-line args' error.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (iarg+2 > narg) error->all(FLERR,"Invalid Kokkos command-line args");' as the first statement of the 't'/'threads' branch.

summary: The 'Kokkos package already initialized' check tests a freshly default-constructed InitializationSettings object, so the branch is dead and the warning can never fire.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:297-310: 'Kokkos::InitializationSettings args;' immediately followed by 'if (args.has_num_threads()) { ... error->warning(FLERR,"Kokkos package already initalized. Cannot change parameters"); nthreads = args.get_num_threads(); ... }'. 'args' is a local object that has just been default constructed and no setter has been called, so has_num_threads() is always false and only the else branch (set_num_threads/set_device_id) ever executes. The comment above it ('we cannot change any Kokkos library parameters after the first initalization') shows the intent was to detect an already-initialized Kokkos runtime, which is what KokkosLMP::initialize() tests with Kokkos::is_initialized() at line 496.
failure_scenario: A library user calls lammps_open() twice with different '-k on t N g M' settings: the second instance silently reports and uses the newly requested nthreads/ngpus in its log while Kokkos keeps the settings from the first initialization (KokkosLMP::initialize skips Kokkos::initialize), and no warning is printed.
suggested_fix: Test 'Kokkos::is_initialized()' (and query the live execution space / init_ngpus) instead of args.has_num_threads(), or drop the dead branch.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 07
summary: The block that reverts the pair/only sort and atom-map overrides is guarded by 'if (lmp->pair_only_flag)' instead of '!lmp->pair_only_flag', so it runs right after the block that set them (cancelling the override) and never when pair/only is switched off.
evidence: kokkos.cpp:776-785 sets sort_legacy/atom_map_legacy=1 with *_changed=1 under pair_only_flag; 824-833 immediately resets them to 0 under the same condition; the analogous comm block at 789 is correctly guarded with '!lmp->pair_only_flag'.
failure_scenario: 'package kokkos pair/only on' never moves sorting and the atom map to the host as intended.
suggested_fix: Change the guard on line 824 to !lmp->pair_only_flag.

summary: The KOKKOS package citation string contains a non-ASCII EN DASH (U+2013) in the BibTeX page range, violating the project's 7-bit US-ASCII rule for a string that is written verbatim to the user's log.cite file.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:66-75:
  static const char cite_kokkos_package[] =
    "KOKKOS package: https://doi.org/10.1145/3731599.3767498\n\n"
    "@inproceedings{Johansson25,\n"
    ...
    " pages = {1217-1232},\n"      <- the dash here is actually U+2013 (bytes e2 80 93)
  }
and src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:518:
  if (lmp->citeme) lmp->citeme->add(cite_kokkos_package);
so the byte sequence is emitted into log.cite.  Detected with `LC_ALL=C grep -n '[^ -~\t]' src/KOKKOS/*` (progress_rules_D/rule7_nonascii.out); the project rule is stated in .github/copilot-instructions.md ('7-bit US-ASCII everywhere (sources, docs, scripts); Unicode is forbidden').  Note `cd src && make check` does NOT catch this: src/Makefile:435 runs only check-whitespace, check-permissions, check-homepage, check-errordocs, check-fmtlib and check-docs, and doc/Makefile's char_check scans only doc/src.
failure_scenario: A user's log.cite contains a UTF-8 en dash; BibTeX/BibLaTeX runs in a plain 8-bit-Latin pipeline render it as garbage ('1217â€“1232'), and any downstream tool that assumes ASCII input on the LAMMPS sources (the stated security policy) flags the file.
suggested_fix: Replace the U+2013 with a plain ASCII hyphen (or the BibTeX page-range idiom '1217--1232').

summary: The order parameter is divided by nnn instead of by the actual neighbour count ncount, so 'nnn NULL' (nnn == 0) divides by zero and yields NaN/Inf for every atom; the CPU style divides by ncount.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_hexorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:268-269 'd_qnarray(i,0) = usum/nnn;\n  d_qnarray(i,1) = vsum/nnn;' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_hexorder_atom.cpp:234-235 'qn[0] = usum/ncount;\n      qn[1] = vsum/ncount;'. The CPU style also guards the empty case at :208 'if ((ncount < nnn) || (ncount == 0)) { qn[0] = qn[1] = 0.0; continue; }', while the KOKKOS kernel only tests 'if (ncount < nnn)' (:240). With nnn == 0 the parser sets nnn = 0 for the 'nnn NULL' keyword (compute_hexorder_atom.cpp:70-71).
failure_scenario: 'compute h all hexorder/atom/kk nnn NULL cutoff 1.5' writes 0.0/0.0 = NaN (or usum/0 = +-Inf) into both columns of c_h for every atom, and the same input on the CPU style returns the correctly averaged order parameter.
suggested_fix: Divide by ncount as the CPU style does (ncount already equals nnn when nnn > 0), and add the 'ncount == 0' early-out to the guard at line 240.

summary: Per-atom scratch d_distsq/d_nearest is allocated as a full inum x maxneigh device array instead of the single maxneigh-sized buffer used by the CPU style.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_hexorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:181-184 'd_distsq = typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d("hexorder/atom:distsq",inum,maxneigh_kk); d_nearest = typename AT::t_int_2d(...,inum,maxneigh_kk);' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_hexorder_atom.cpp:182-183 'memory->create(distsq,maxneigh,...); memory->create(nearest,maxneigh,...);' (one row total). Same shape as src/KOKKOS/compute_centro_atom_kokkos.cpp:121-124.
failure_scenario: Large systems with dense neighbour lists need natoms*maxneigh extra device words and can exhaust GPU memory where the CPU style needs a few kB.
suggested_fix: Use team/thread scratch memory or process atoms in bounded chunks.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 04, line corrected)
summary: The hexatic order parameter is divided by nnn instead of ncount and the ncount==0 guard is missing, so 'nnn NULL' (nnn=0) yields NaN/Inf for every atom.
evidence: compute_hexorder_atom_kokkos.cpp:163 'if (ncount < nnn)' (no ncount==0 test), 191-192 'd_qnarray(i,0) = usum/nnn; d_qnarray(i,1) = vsum/nnn;' vs src/EXTRA-COMPUTE/compute_hexorder_atom.cpp qn[0] = usum/ncount with an (ncount==0) early-out.
failure_scenario: compute hexorder/atom/kk nnn NULL cutoff R: 0/0 = NaN in both columns for every atom; CPU style returns the correct average.
suggested_fix: Divide by ncount and add the ncount == 0 early-out.

summary: The per-type mass array is read on the device without ever syncing atomKK->k_mass, which is only ever marked modify_host(), so on a GPU the kernel reads a zero-initialized device view and every atom's kinetic energy comes out as 0.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_electron_stopping_kokkos.cpp:41 lists `X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | TYPE_MASK | TAG_MASK | MASK_MASK | RMASS_MASK` -- there is no mask bit for the per-type mass -- and line 84 does `d_mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();`, used at line 143 `double massone = (d_rmass.data()) ? ... : static_cast<double>(d_mass(itype));` inside the device kernel. `grep -n 'k_mass' src/KOKKOS/fix_electron_stopping_kokkos.cpp` returns only line 84: no sync anywhere. k_mass is only ever marked host-modified (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:313-316 and the set_mass overloads at 287,293,299,305), so every consumer must sync it itself; the correct idiom is src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46 `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();`, and it is followed by compute_temp_kokkos.cpp:46, compute_ke_atom_kokkos.cpp:68, group_kokkos.h:64, fix_flow_gauss_kokkos.cpp etc. The CPU base reads the host array directly: src/EXTRA-FIX/fix_electron_stopping.cpp:172 `double massone = (atom->rmass) ? atom->rmass[i] : atom->mass[itype];`.
failure_scenario: GPU run of `fix electron/stopping/kk` on a per-type-mass atom style (the normal case for the radiation-damage workflows this fix targets) without another /kk style that happens to sync k_mass first: d_mass(itype) reads the zero-filled device allocation, so energy = 0.5*mvv2e*0*v2 = 0, every atom fails the `energy < Ecut` test and NO electronic stopping force is ever applied -- the fix silently does nothing and SeLoss stays 0.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();` in FixElectronStoppingKokkos::init() (or right before line 84), as fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46 does.

summary: The region test is applied before the energy checks instead of after them, so an atom outside the region whose kinetic energy exceeds the stopping table no longer triggers the 'kinetic energy too high' error that the CPU fix raises.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_electron_stopping_kokkos.cpp:138-152 orders the tests mask -> numneigh -> `if (region && !d_match(i)) return;` -> energy -> `if (energy > d_elstop_ranges(0, table_entries-1)) { error_value = {i, energy}; return; }`. The CPU base does the opposite and says so explicitly: src/EXTRA-FIX/fix_electron_stopping.cpp:165-185 `// Do fast checks first, only then the region check` -- mask (166), numneigh (169), energy vs table max with `error->one(...)` (178-180), and only then `if (region) { if (region->match(...) != 1) continue; }` (182-185).
failure_scenario: An input with `fix electron/stopping ... region <r>` where a fast atom outside region r exceeds the tabulated energy range: the CPU fix aborts with 'kinetic energy too high for atom N', the /kk fix runs on silently. Forces are identical in both cases, so this only changes whether the user is told the table is too short.
suggested_fix: Move the `if (region && !d_match(i)) return;` test to after the `energy > d_elstop_ranges(0, table_entries-1)` check so the two versions raise the same error, or note the intentional difference in a comment.

summary: fix electron/stopping/kk reads per-type mass on the device without syncing atomKK->k_mass.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_electron_stopping_kokkos.cpp:84-85 `d_mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>(); d_rmass = atomKK->k_rmass.view<DeviceType>();` and line 143 `double massone = (d_rmass.data()) ? ... : static_cast<double>(d_mass(itype));`.  The file carefully syncs its own DualViews (k_elstop_ranges line 51, k_match line 102) and the per-atom masks (line 72 `atomKK->sync(execution_space, datamask_read)`), but never `k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()`; mass has no mask bit (src/atom_masks.h) and is host-modified only (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:287-316).
failure_scenario: GPU run with per-type masses and no other style syncing k_mass: massone is 0, so the kinetic energy `0.5*mv^2` used to look up the electronic stopping table is 0 and no stopping force is ever applied (silently wrong physics rather than a crash).
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: BondHybridKokkos::compute() calls modify_device() on a subview that shares its DualView modified-flags with the parent, which starves a partial_flag sub-style (quartic/kk) of its host-side bond-type-zero writes and then overwrites them.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:117-119 'auto k_bondlist_m = Kokkos::subview(k_bondlist,m,Kokkos::ALL,Kokkos::ALL); k_bondlist_m.modify_device(); neighborKK->k_bondlist = k_bondlist_m;'. Kokkos DualView subviews share the modified_flags view, so modify_device() sets modified_flags(1) > modified_flags(0) every step. bond quartic/kk marks broken bonds by writing the HOST mirror and calling modify_host: src/KOKKOS/bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:202 'h_bondlist(n,2) = 0;' and :249 'neighborKK->k_bondlist.modify_host();'. On the following step the hybrid's modify_device() at :118 makes modified_device > modified_host, so quartic's 'neighborKK->k_bondlist.template sync<DeviceType>()' (bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:112) performs NO H2D copy and its 'sync_host()' (:180) instead copies device->host, wiping the zeros. Standalone quartic/kk does not hit this because nothing calls modify_device on the neighbor bondlist.
failure_scenario: 'bond_style hybrid/kk quartic/kk harmonic/kk' + chain scission: within one reneighbor interval the bondlist entry of a broken bond is restored to its original type every step, so the 'if (bondlist(n,2) <= 0) return;' skip (bond_quartic_kokkos.cpp:266) never fires; if the two atoms relax back inside rc before the next reneighbor the bond is silently re-formed, whereas the CPU bond_hybrid keeps it broken permanently.
suggested_fix: Do not call modify_device() on the shared subview flags; instead give each sub-style bondlist its own DualView (or clear/restore the flags per sub-style) and honour the sub-style's modify_host by syncing the sub-list back to the device before the next step.

summary: BondHybridKokkos::compute() omits the partial_flag / orig_map write-back that the CPU BondHybrid uses to propagate deleted (type 0) bonds from the sub-style bondlist back into the original neighbor bondlist.
evidence: CPU src/bond_hybrid.cpp:85-88 allocates orig_map[m], :99 'if (partial_flag) orig_map[m][n] = i;', and :148-157 'if (partial_flag) { ... if (bondlist[m][i][2] <= 0) { n = orig_map[m][i]; bondlist_orig[n][2] = bondlist[m][i][2]; } }'. The KOKKOS version src/KOKKOS/bond_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:96-103 builds the sub-style lists with no orig_map, and :145-148 restores the original list ('neighbor->nbondlist = nbondlist_orig; neighborKK->k_bondlist = k_bondlist_orig;') without any write-back. partial_flag is set by bond quartic (src/MOLECULE/bond_quartic.cpp:39 'partial_flag = 1;') and bond quartic/kk inherits it, and quartic/kk is a legal hybrid/kk sub-style (bond_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:194-196 only requires kokkosable).
failure_scenario: 'bond_style hybrid/kk quartic/kk ...': after a bond breaks, neighbor->bondlist still carries the old nonzero bond type until the next reneighbor, so 'compute bond/local' / 'compute bond' report a finite energy and length for a bond that the CPU version reports as deleted.
suggested_fix: Port the partial_flag path: keep a per-sub-style orig_map device view filled in the second parallel_for and, when any sub-style has partial_flag, scatter type<=0 entries back into k_bondlist_orig after the sub-style loop.

summary: In the Device branch of AtomVecSpinKokkos::sync_pinned the guard for the fm array tests k_sp instead of k_fm, so fm can be left unsynced (or synced spuriously) depending on the state of an unrelated array.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_spin_kokkos.cpp:289-294: 'if ((mask & SP_MASK) && atomKK->k_sp.need_sync_device()) perform_pinned_copy_transform<DAT::ttransform_kkfloat_1d_4>(atomKK->k_sp,space,async_flag); if ((mask & FM_MASK) && atomKK->k_sp.need_sync_device()) perform_pinned_copy_transform<DAT::ttransform_kkacc_1d_3>(atomKK->k_fm,space,async_flag); if ((mask & FML_MASK) && atomKK->k_fm_long.need_sync_device()) ...'. The FM line tests k_sp, not k_fm. The host branch of the same function has it right: src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_spin_kokkos.cpp:312-313 'if ((mask & FM_MASK) && atomKK->k_fm.need_sync_host()) perform_pinned_copy_transform<DAT::ttransform_kkacc_1d_3>(atomKK->k_fm,space,async_flag);'. The reference implementation always pairs the guard with the view it copies (src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_atomic_kokkos.cpp:165-179).
failure_scenario: Whenever a caller asks for sync_pinned(Device, ... FM_MASK ...) with fm modified on the host and sp already clean, fm is not copied to the device and the following spin kernel reads stale magnetic forces. Today only sync_pinned(HostKK,...)/sync_pinned(Host,...) call sites exist (verlet_kokkos.cpp:448, dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:230, third_order_kokkos.cpp:230), so the defect is latent, but it is armed for the first Device-side caller.
suggested_fix: Change the FM_MASK guard on line 291 to 'atomKK->k_fm.need_sync_device()'.

summary: AtomVecSpinKokkos::force_clear() ignores its first argument, so it always zeroes fm/fm_long starting at atom 0 instead of at atom n as the base class does.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_spin_kokkos.cpp:166-190: 'void AtomVecSpinKokkos::force_clear(int /*n*/, size_t nbytes) { int nzero = (double)nbytes/sizeof(double); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(nzero, LAMMPS_LAMBDA(int i) { l_fm(i,0) = 0.0; ... l_fm_long(i,2) = 0.0; }); ... }'. The base is src/SPIN/atom_vec_spin.cpp:86-90: 'void AtomVecSpin::force_clear(int n, size_t nbytes) { memset(&fm[n][0], 0, 3 * nbytes); memset(&fm_long[n][0], 0, 3 * nbytes); }' -- it starts at row n. The interface contract is stated in src/atom_vec.h:74 and in the comment 'clear extra forces starting at atom N'.
failure_scenario: Latent today: the only KOKKOS caller, MinKokkos::force_clear (src/KOKKOS/min_kokkos.cpp:602-606), passes n = 0. Any future caller that uses the neighbor->includegroup form (src/verlet.cpp:417 calls 'atom->avec->force_clear(nlocal,nbytes)') would zero the wrong atoms and clobber the magnetic forces of the first nlocal atoms while leaving the ghosts stale.
suggested_fix: Honour the argument: capture n and zero rows [n, n+nzero) (or assert n == 0 with an explicit comment if the offset form is deliberately unsupported).

summary: Same defect as pair_born_coul_wolf_kokkos: the Wolf self-energy is summed on the host from `atom->q[i]` while compute() only syncs q to the device, so the charges are stale on a GPU build after any device-side exchange or atom sort.
failure_scenario: Multi-rank GPU run with `pair_style born/coul/wolf/cs/kk`: the self-energy term of eng_coul is computed from the previous step's host charges after atoms migrate.
suggested_fix: Compute the self-energy in the device kernel from the `q` device view (cf. pair_coul_wolf_cs_kokkos.cpp:239-243), or sync Q_MASK to the host and loop over list->ilist.

summary: The Device branch of AtomVecFullKokkos::sync_pinned omits k_dihedral_atom4 (same copy-paste defect as the molecular style).
failure_scenario: Same as the molecular case: a Device-space pinned sync of DIHEDRAL_MASK leaves dihedral_atom4 stale on the GPU for atom_style full/kk.
suggested_fix: Add the missing k_dihedral_atom4 entry to the Device branch.

summary: The five MS-MEAM per-atom arrays and their duplicated scatter views are allocated unconditionally, where the CPU base allocates them only when msmeamflag is set, wasting 23 KK_FLOATs per atom (times the thread count under a duplicated scatter view) in every plain pair_style meam/kk run.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/meam_dens_init_kokkos.h:148-168 allocates k_arho2mb (nmax), k_arho1m (nmax x 3), k_arho2m (nmax x 6), k_arho3m (nmax x 10) and k_arho3mb (nmax x 3) with no msmeamflag test, and :222-226 / :237-241 unconditionally build dup_/ndup_ scatter views over them ('dup_arho2mb = Kokkos::Experimental::create_scatter_view<...ScatterDuplicated>(d_arho2mb);' etc.), with :261-265 contributing them back. The CPU original guards every one of these: src/MEAM/meam_dens_init.cpp:74-81 'if (msmeamflag) { memory->create(arho1m, nmax, 3, "pair:arho1m"); memory->create(arho2m, nmax, 6, ...); memory->create(arho3m, nmax, 10, ...); memory->create(arho2mb, nmax, ...); memory->create(arho3mb, nmax, 3, ...); }' (and the matching destroy at :47-53). Every consumer of these arrays in the KOKKOS kernels is itself behind 'if (msmeamflag)' (meam_dens_init_kokkos.h:47-63, :516-523, :561-570, :578-598), so the storage is provably dead for a non-MS-MEAM potential.
failure_scenario: pair_style meam/kk (not meam/ms/kk) on a GPU with 10 million owned+ghost atoms permanently holds an extra 23 * 8 bytes/atom = ~1.8 GB of device memory that is never read or written; on a threaded host backend where lmp->kokkos->need_dup<DeviceType>() is true the duplicated scatter views multiply that waste by the thread count, so a 16-thread run over 1M atoms burns ~2.9 GB.
suggested_fix: Wrap the msmeam allocations at :148-168, the scatter-view creation at :221-226 / :236-241, and the contribute calls at :260-265 in 'if (msmeamflag)', mirroring src/MEAM/meam_dens_init.cpp:74-81.

summary: atomKK->modified() for X_MASK|V_MASK is called before the reflection kernels run instead of after them, so a host-side sync triggered from inside the wall loop (equal-style wall variable) clears the device-modified flag and the reflections of the remaining walls are never copied back to the host.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_reflect_kokkos.cpp:48-49 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,datamask_read); atomKK->modified(execution_space,datamask_modify);' -- the parallel_for that actually writes x and v is only issued later, at lines 77-79 inside the 'for (int m = 0; m < nwall; m++)' loop, and line 65 evaluates 'input->variable->compute_equal(varindex[m])' between the modified() call and the last kernel. Every other Kokkos fix in the package calls modified() after the kernels, e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_setforce_kokkos.cpp:110-145 and src/KOKKOS/fix_momentum_kokkos.cpp:121-129, and the sibling style src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_piston_kokkos.cpp:164-203 does the same.
failure_scenario: 'fix w all wall/reflect/kk xlo 0.0 xhi v_top' where the equal-style variable v_top references a compute or thermo keyword that reads per-atom x on the host: evaluating the variable syncs x device->host and clears k_x's device-modified flag; the subsequent xhi reflection kernel then writes only the device copy, and the following host read (dump, another non-kokkos fix) sees unreflected coordinates.
suggested_fix: Move 'atomKK->modified(execution_space,datamask_modify);' to after the wall loop (just before the addstep_compute call).

summary: pace/extrapolation/kk scales the pair forces with scale(itype,itype) while the CPU base scales them with scale[itype][jtype], so a non-uniform 'scale' (fix adapt) gives different forces on the KOKKOS path.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_pace_extrapolation_kokkos.cpp:1429 (TagPairPACEComputeDerivative) 'const KK_FLOAT scale = d_scale(itype,itype);' and :1692-1694 'f_ij(ii, jj, 0) = scale * f_ji[0] + ...'. The CPU base src/ML-PACE/pair_pace_extrapolation.cpp:251-253 uses the OFF-DIAGONAL element: 'fij[0] = scale[itype][jtype] * neighbours_forces(jj, 0);' (only the energy at :276 uses scale[itype][itype]). scale is user-settable per type pair through extract() (src/ML-PACE/pair_pace_extrapolation.cpp:482) i.e. 'fix adapt ... pair pace/extrapolation scale I J v_x'.
failure_scenario: pair_style pace/extrapolation with 'fix adapt pair pace/extrapolation scale 1 2 v_s' and s != scale(1,1): the /kk forces between type-1 and type-2 atoms are scaled by scale(1,1) instead of scale(1,2), giving different (and non-conservative) forces than the non-KOKKOS run.
suggested_fix: In TagPairPACEComputeDerivative read the neighbor's LAMMPS type and use d_scale(itype,jtype) for f_ij, keeping d_scale(itype,itype) for the energy tally, matching the base class.

summary: VerletKokkos::operator()(const int&) and the 'f' view member are dead code -- the force merge uses the free ForceAdder functor, and nothing ever launches a kernel with *this.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.h:41-49 declares 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void operator() (const int& i) const {f(i,0) += f_merge_copy(i,0); ...}' and 'DAT::t_kkacc_1d_3 f_merge_copy,f;'.  The only merge in the .cpp is verlet_kokkos.cpp:515-516 'Kokkos::parallel_for(atomKK->k_f.extent(0), ForceAdder<DAT::t_kkacc_1d_3,DAT::t_kkacc_1d_3>(atomKK->k_f.view_device(),f_merge_copy));' using the file-static ForceAdder (verlet_kokkos.cpp:36-48); 'f' is only ever assigned (verlet_kokkos.cpp:512 'f = atomKK->k_f.view_device();') and never read.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; the member keeps a reference to the force view alive and the unused operator() invites confusion about which functor the merge uses.
suggested_fix: Remove the operator() and the 'f' member (and the assignment at verlet_kokkos.cpp:512), keeping only f_merge_copy.

summary: sna_kokkos.h declares three member functions and one data member that have no definition and no caller anywhere in the tree.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos.h:482-486 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION void create_team_scratch_arrays(const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type& team); ... void create_thread_scratch_arrays(const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type& team);' and :246-247 'KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION SNAKokkos(const SNAKokkos<DeviceType, real_type, accum_type, vector_length>& sna, const typename Kokkos::TeamPolicy<DeviceType>::member_type& team);' -- none of the three is defined in sna_kokkos_impl.h nor referenced anywhere ('grep -rn create_team_scratch_arrays src/' matches only this declaration). :409 'int twojmax, diagonalstyle;' -- diagonalstyle is never assigned or read (it is a leftover from the removed 'diagonal' SNAP option).
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; dead declarations mislead readers into thinking there is a team-scratch constructor path, and the uninitialized diagonalstyle member is a false lead when debugging.
suggested_fix: Delete the three declarations and the diagonalstyle member.

summary: improper fourier/kk allocates a brand-new Kokkos DualView for the warning flag on every timestep inside compute() instead of once in the constructor.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/improper_fourier_kokkos.cpp:99-105 inside compute(): `// zero warning flag` / `k_warning_flag = DAT::tdual_int_scalar("ImproperFourier::warning_flag");` / `d_warning_flag = k_warning_flag.template view<DeviceType>();` / `h_warning_flag = k_warning_flag.view_host();` / `h_warning_flag() = 0; ...`. The constructor (:36-47) does not create it, unlike every other KOKKOS bonded style: improper_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:46-48 and improper_class2_kokkos.cpp:44-46 create it once in the ctor and only zero it per step. improper_umbrella_kokkos.cpp:97-103 has the same defect.
failure_scenario: Every MD step with improper_style fourier/kk performs a device allocation and free (cudaMalloc/cudaFree class of call) that serializes the GPU stream; overhead only, no wrong numbers.
suggested_fix: Move the k_warning_flag / d_warning_flag / h_warning_flag initialization into the ImproperFourierKokkos constructor and keep only the zero+modify_host+sync in compute().

summary: Error message in PairTersoffMODKokkos::init_style names the wrong pair style ("pair tersoff/kk" instead of tersoff/mod/kk), a copy-paste leftover from pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:120-121 `if (neighflag == FULL)\n    error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair tersoff/kk");` -- identical string to src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:134-135.
failure_scenario: User runs `pair_style tersoff/mod/kk` with `-pk kokkos neigh full`; the error names a style they are not using, sending them to the wrong input line.
suggested_fix: Change the string to name tersoff/mod/kk (and check the same copy in pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp / pair_tersoff_mod_c_kokkos.cpp).
